newsitem.title: GERMANY: Analysts comments on Krupp bid for Thyssen.
newsitem.headline: Analysts comments on Krupp bid for Thyssen.

text.p: Following are comments from analysts about Fried. Krupp Krupp-Hoesch AG's announcement it would make a 435 marks per share offer for Thyssen AG.
Shares in Thyssen, which were suspended from regular trade but have been changing hands in unofficial trade, jumped on the news to a new high of 410 marks immediately after the annoucement.
"The offer by Krupp at first glance is a bit above expectations. But it will be difficult for Thyssen to fight this offer in a short period of time.
"It will be critical for Thyssen to make its shareholders believe that the company is worth more than this amount.

"I had valued Thyssen shares at 370 marks on core activities and after the divestment of loss-making units. But their participation in the E-plus mobile network adds another 80 marks or so to the share price and real estate reserves add another minimum 20 marks per share.
"The E-plus stake can be sold and the profit potential from core activities is still not proven at the moment. But it will be realised in the next two to three years."
Peter Fish, of MEPS, an industry analyst group based in Sheffield, England:

"It's a sort of a reverse takeover. I thought it would have been the other way around. Having said that, I think it comes together out of necessity. Rationalisation is needed at both companies and I am certain that could occur only by making bigger units, particularly in Germany.
"I think what we are left with the mainly flat-steel production companies coming together."

"There is a lot of industrial logic in such a deal. The companies have a lot of synergies and produce a similar range of products that can molded together and achieve major rationalisation particularly within overhead and sales structures. That's the key to this deal."
